chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: Regarding a man who buys food of a specific village, and if he does not specify a particular village for him, he gives him from wherever he wishes.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a buyer purchases unspecified food without naming a specific source?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the validity of selling unspecified bulk food (*al-ma'kool*) when the source is not explicitly defined, granting the seller discretion to deliver from any village. It highlights the practical flexibility in commercial transactions within Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that ambiguity in origin does not invalidate the contract as long as the quality and quantity are agreed upon. This ruling supports the broader principle that *bay' al-ma'kool* is permissible provided the essential elements of the sale are clear.
